renderModes.description: Tempo.Blazor supports all Blazor render modes.

modes.name: InteractiveWebAssembly
modes.description: Full client-side rendering in the browser via WebAssembly.

modes.name: InteractiveServer
modes.description: Server-side rendering with SignalR connection for interactivity.

modes.name: InteractiveAuto
modes.description: Starts with Server rendering, switches to WebAssembly once downloaded. Recommended for best UX.

renderModes.notes: Components with JS interop (dashboard, workflow designer, rich editor, scheduler, PDF viewer, diagram editor, color picker, file manager, Gantt, Notion editor, document editor, signing, spreadsheet, wireframe designer, and email variable insertion) gracefully degrade during prerendering and activate once the client-side runtime is available.

cssFramework.description: Tempo.Blazor uses its own standalone CSS framework based on CSS custom properties (design tokens). No external CSS framework (like Bootstrap or Tailwind) is required. The library ships a single tempo-blazor.bundled.css file that includes all component styles, design tokens, base resets, and animations.
cssFramework.architecture: The CSS is organized as: tokens (design variables) → base resets → component styles. Each component uses BEM-like class naming with the tm- prefix (e.g., tm-btn, tm-data-table, tm-modal__header).

darkMode.description: Dark mode is supported via CSS custom property overrides. Activate by adding data-theme="dark" attribute or .tm-dark class to a parent element (typically <html> or <body>).
darkMode.themeService: Use the ThemeService (registered via DI) to toggle themes programmatically.

designTokens.description: All visual properties are controlled via CSS custom properties (--tm-*). Override these to customize the look and feel without modifying component CSS.

colorPrimary.description: Primary brand color palette (blue by default)

borders.description: Border colors. --tm-border-color is the decorative divider tone; the boundary of a selection control (checkbox, radio, multiselect option), which conveys the control's state, uses --tm-border-color-control so it stays above the WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 minimum. Retheming a control must go through the -control token, not through --tm-border-color. --tm-control-hover-fill is the fill an UNCHECKED control takes while hovered: the hover used to recolour the outline only, which is a hue change of ~1.05:1 and therefore invisible in greyscale. A palette override must keep the hovered outline (--tm-color-primary) at 3:1 against this fill.

typography.description: Font families, sizes, weights, and line heights

tokens.--tm-font-mono: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Code', 'Source Code Pro', Menlo, monospace

customization.description: Override design tokens in your app CSS to customize the theme globally.

localization.description: Tempo.Blazor supports localization via the ITmLocalizer interface (namespace Tempo.Blazor.Localization, defined in Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions). All built-in component UI strings (button labels, tooltips, placeholders, validation messages, aria-labels, etc.) go through this interface. The library ships with 500+ localization keys covering all components.

architecture.interface: ITmLocalizer — two indexer overloads: this[string key] for simple lookups, this[string key, params object[] arguments] for formatted strings (e.g. Loc["TmImageGallery_Counter", 5, 20] → "5 of 20").
architecture.defaultImplementation: DefaultTmLocalizer (internal) — backed by IStringLocalizer<TmResources> using embedded .resx files (TmResources.resx for English, TmResources.cs.resx for Czech).
architecture.injection: All components get the localizer via @inject ITmLocalizer Loc in the library's _Imports.razor. Components then use Loc["KeyName"] in markup and code.
architecture.registration: AddTempoBlazor() registers: (1) ITmLocalizer as Singleton (stateless, thread-safe, backed by .resx), (2) ThemeService as Scoped (per-circuit in Server, per-tab in WASM), (3) ToastService as Scoped (per-circuit in Server, per-tab in WASM). Uses TryAdd* so your custom registrations take precedence if registered AFTER AddTempoBlazor().

localization.keyNamingConvention: Keys follow the pattern Tm[ComponentName]_[Action/State]. Shared keys use Tm_ prefix (e.g. Tm_Save, Tm_Cancel, Tm_Loading). Component-specific keys include the component name (e.g. TmDataTable_NoResults, TmRichEditor_Bold, TmFilterBuilder_Contains).

switchLanguage.description: Set the culture in Program.cs before builder.Build(). This makes IStringLocalizer pick the correct .resx file automatically.

customLocalizer.description: To fully replace all component strings (e.g. for a language not shipped with the library), implement ITmLocalizer and register it AFTER AddTempoBlazor(). The TryAddSingleton in AddTempoBlazor() will be skipped if your registration comes first.

partialOverride.description: To override only specific keys while keeping the rest from the built-in resources, create a decorator that falls back to the default implementation.

addNewLanguage.description: To add a new language (e.g. German), implement ITmLocalizer with all keys translated. You can export the English .resx keys as a reference. Since DefaultTmLocalizer is internal, a full custom implementation is the recommended approach for new languages.

items.description: Block-based WYSIWYG markdown editor (Notion-inspired). The user edits rich formatted content — bold, italic, headings, lists, links, code — with no markdown syntax ever visible. The Value parameter is a raw Markdown string (input and output). Internally each paragraph, heading, or list item is a separate block div; inline formatting uses real semantic HTML elements (<b>, <em>, <s>, <code>, <a>). Supports Ctrl+Enter submit, character limit, link dialog, and keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+K).

items.description: Pure SVG chart component supporting Bar, Line, Area, Pie, Donut, and HorizontalBar chart types with optional legend, grid, value labels, animation, gradient area fills, a proportional DateTime X axis for time series, combo charts (per-dataset ChartDataset.RenderAs = ChartDatasetRenderAs.Line renders that dataset as a line overlay over the bars of a Bar chart on a shared Y scale — bars for periodic flows, lines for cumulative values), dense-axis label thinning on Bar charts (over 24 categories only every n-th label renders), negative values on Bar/Line charts (signed domain with an emphasized zero axis; bars grow down from the zero baseline), point-marker thinning on dense line series (markers closer than ~9 units thin to ~24-unit spacing while the polyline stays complete), and click events on segments. Stacked variants (StackedBar vertical, StackedHorizontalBar, StackedArea) accumulate each category's datasets on a shared baseline scaled to the largest stack total; non-positive values contribute nothing to a stack, datasets toggle off through the series legend, and bar value labels are omitted when a segment is too small to keep the text readable.

examples.title: Reorderable board persisting position
examples.code:
<TmKanbanBoard TItem="TaskItem"
               Items="@tasks"
               Columns="@columns"
               ColumnSelector="t => t.Status"
               CardTemplate="RenderCard"
               OnItemMoved="HandleMove"
               OnItemReordered="HandleMove" />

@code {
    void HandleMove(KanbanMoveEvent<TaskItem> e)
    {
        var moved = e.Item with { Status = e.ToColumn };
        tasks.RemoveAll(t => t.Id == e.Item.Id);
        var at = e.TargetBeforeItem is not null
            ? tasks.FindIndex(t => t.Id == e.TargetBeforeItem.Id)
            : tasks.Count;
        tasks.Insert(at < 0 ? tasks.Count : at, moved);
    }
}

examples.title: Swimlanes grouped by assignee
examples.code:
<TmKanbanBoard TItem="TaskItem"
               Items="@tasks"
               Columns="@columns"
               ColumnSelector="t => t.Status"
               SwimlaneSelector="t => string.IsNullOrEmpty(t.Assignee) ? null : t.Assignee"
               CardTemplate="RenderCard"
               OnItemMoved="HandleMove"
               OnItemReordered="HandleReorder" />

@code {
    // e.ToSwimlane is the target assignee (null = unassigned / "no value" lane)
    void HandleMove(KanbanMoveEvent<TaskItem> e)
        => Apply(e, e.Item with { Status = e.ToColumn, Assignee = e.ToSwimlane ?? "" });
}

    // DisplayResolver flows from TmViewManager → TmFilterBuilder → TmFilterChip.
    // Usually you set DisplayResolver on the parent TmDataTable or TmMultiViewList
    // and it flows automatically. Direct usage shown here for standalone scenarios.
    private string? ResolveDisplay(string fieldName, string? rawValue)
    {
        if (rawValue is null)
            return fieldName switch { "Status" => "Order Status", "Priority" => "Priority", _ => null };
        return (fieldName, rawValue) switch
        {
            ("Status", "Pending") => "Pending",
            ("Status", "Shipped") => "Shipped",
            ("Status", "Delivered") => "Delivered",
            _ => null
        };
    }
}

@code {
    private string? _ownerLogin;

    private async Task<TmPickerSearchResult<UserDto>> SearchUsersAsync(string query, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        try
        {
            var users = await UserService.SearchAsync(query, ct);
            return new TmPickerSearchResult<UserDto>(users, users.Count == 0 ? TmPickerFetchState.Empty : TmPickerFetchState.Ok);
        }
        catch (Exception) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            return new TmPickerSearchResult<UserDto>([], TmPickerFetchState.Transient);
        }
    }

    private async Task<TmPickerResolveResult<UserDto>> ResolveUserAsync(string login, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        try
        {
            var user = await UserService.GetByLoginAsync(login, ct);
            return new TmPickerResolveResult<UserDto>(user, TmPickerFetchState.Ok);
        }
        catch (Exception) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            return new TmPickerResolveResult<UserDto>(default, TmPickerFetchState.Transient);
        }
    }
}

parameters.name: HeaderLeading
parameters.description: Optional content rendered immediately BEFORE the tab strip, as a SIBLING of the role="tablist" element — never inside it. The tab strip owns a roving tabindex (Arrow/Home/End, tabindex 0/-1, aria-selected AND the DOM focus, which moves with the selection); an element that can never be selected would misreport that contract to assistive technology and would be reachable with the arrow keys as if it were a tab. Setting this (or HeaderTrailing) wraps the strip in an extra .tm-tabs__header-row flex row. The wrapper is emitted ONLY when at least one slot is supplied; with neither slot the rendered markup is byte-identical to a tab strip that has no slots at all, so existing CSS and tests that rely on .tm-tabs > .tm-tabs__header keep working. CONTRACT FOR STICKY CONSUMERS: when the slots are in use, a sticky tab strip must stick the ROW (.tm-tabs__header-row), not the header (.tm-tabs__header). Sticking the header alone pins only the strip and lets the slot content scroll away.

parameters.name: HeaderTrailing
parameters.description: Optional content rendered immediately AFTER the tab strip, as a SIBLING of the role="tablist" element — never inside it, for the same roving-focus reason as HeaderLeading. Setting this (or HeaderLeading) wraps the strip in an extra .tm-tabs__header-row flex row. The wrapper is emitted ONLY when at least one slot is supplied; with neither slot the rendered markup is byte-identical to a tab strip that has no slots at all. CONTRACT FOR STICKY CONSUMERS: when the slots are in use, stick the ROW (.tm-tabs__header-row), not the header (.tm-tabs__header), otherwise the slot content scrolls away from under the pinned strip.

libraryExamples.description: Implement dark mode toggle using ThemeService and the built-in dark theme tokens. ThemeService is a simple in-memory service with IsDark, ThemeName, Toggle(), and an OnChanged event.
libraryExamples.setupNote: The dark theme is defined in tokens-dark.css and activates when [data-theme="dark"] or .tm-dark class is set on a parent element. ThemeService has: IsDark (bool), ThemeName ("dark"/"light"), Toggle(), OnChanged (event). ThemeService is automatically registered as Scoped by AddTempoBlazor(). For InteractiveAuto, call AddTempoBlazor() in both Server and Client Program.cs. For app-wide dark mode, set data-theme on <html> or your root layout element.

<TmToolbar Title="Employees" Sticky="true">

        <TmToolbarButton Icon="@IconNames.Filter" Text="Filters"
            OnClick="() => _showFilters = !_showFilters" />
        <TmToolbarButton Icon="@IconNames.Download" Text="Export"

        <TmToolbarDivider />
        <TmToolbarButton Icon="@IconNames.Plus" Text="New Employee"
            Variant="ButtonVariant.Primary" OnClick="OpenCreateForm" />
    </Actions>

@if (_showFilters)
{
    <TmFilterBuilder FilterDefinitions="@_filterDefs" ActiveFilters="@_activeFilters"

<TmDataTable TItem="EmployeeDto" DataProvider="@_dataProvider" ViewContext="employees"
    Selectable="true" ShowGrouping="true"
    OnRowClick="OpenEditForm" OnSelectionChanged="sel => _selected = sel.ToList()">

        <TmButton Variant="ButtonVariant.Ghost" OnClick="ExportSelected">
            <TmIcon Name="@IconNames.Download" Size="IconSize.Sm" /> Export
        </TmButton>
        <TmButton Variant="ButtonVariant.Danger" OnClick="ConfirmDeleteSelected">
            <TmIcon Name="@IconNames.Trash2" Size="IconSize.Sm" /> Delete

    <TmDataTableColumn Title="Name" Field="e => e.FullName" Sortable="true"
        Filterable="true" Groupable="true" />
    <TmDataTableColumn Title="Department" Field="e => e.Department" Sortable="true"
        Filterable="true" FilterType="FilterType.Select"
        FilterOptions="@_deptOptions" Groupable="true" />
    <TmDataTableColumn Title="Status" Field="e => e.Status">

            <TmBadge Variant="@GetStatusVariant(emp.Status)"
                BadgeStyle="BadgeStyle.Subtle" Dot="true">@emp.Status</TmBadge>
        </CellTemplate>
    </TmDataTableColumn>
    <TmDataTableColumn Title="Hired" Field="e => e.HireDate" Sortable="true"
        Align="ColumnAlign.Right" Width="120px" />
    <TmDataTableColumn Title="" Width="50px" Hideable="false">

                    <TmButton Variant="ButtonVariant.Ghost" Size="ButtonSize.Sm">

libraryExamples.title: Custom Icon Registration
libraryExamples.description: Register custom application-specific icons via IconRegistry in Program.cs. Icons can be registered individually with inline SVG content, or in bulk via a custom IIconProvider implementation.
libraryExamples.usageCode:
@* Use registered custom icons in Razor — reference by the registered name *@
<TmIcon Name="company-logo" Size="IconSize.Lg" />
<TmIcon Name="app-dashboard" Color="IconColor.Primary" />
<TmIcon Name="app-reports" Size="IconSize.Xl" StrokeWidth="1.5" />
libraryExamples.setupNote: Icon resolution order: built-in icons → direct registry (IconRegistry.Register) → IIconProvider providers (in registration order). SVG content must be inner elements only (path, circle, line, rect, polyline, etc.) — NOT the <svg> wrapper. Names are case-insensitive.

libraryExamples.title: Custom Localization — Full Language Override
libraryExamples.description: Replace all component UI strings with your own translations by implementing ITmLocalizer. Register your implementation AFTER AddTempoBlazor() so TryAddSingleton is skipped. The library has 500+ keys following the Tm[Component]_[Action] naming pattern.
libraryExamples.setupNote: ITmLocalizer is defined in Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions (namespace Tempo.Blazor.Localization). The interface has two indexer overloads: this[string key] for simple lookups and this[string key, params object[] arguments] for formatted strings. Keys follow the pattern Tm[ComponentName]_[Action]. Always return the key itself as fallback for unmapped keys to avoid blank UI. Use string.Format for keys with placeholders like TmDataTable_ShowingItems ({0}–{1} of {2}).

libraryExamples.title: Custom Localization — Partial Override (Decorator)
libraryExamples.description: Override only specific localization strings while keeping the rest from the built-in English/Czech resources. Uses a decorator pattern wrapping the default IStringLocalizer<TmResources>.
libraryExamples.setupNote: This approach injects IStringLocalizer<TmResources> (from the built-in .resx files) into your custom localizer. Only the keys in the _overrides dictionary are changed; everything else comes from the default resources. This works with both English and Czech — the built-in IStringLocalizer respects the current CultureInfo.

libraryExamples.title: Switching UI Language at Runtime

libraryExamples.title: TmNavigationGuard - Guard an edit form against unsaved-work loss
libraryExamples.description: Blocks internal router navigation while a form is dirty, showing a TmDialog confirmation, and arms a browser beforeunload prompt for tab close/refresh. Call Suppress() before a post-commit programmatic navigation so the guard does not re-prompt for work that was just saved.
libraryExamples.code:
<TmNavigationGuard @ref="_guard" IsDirty="@_isDirty" OnConfirmLeave="@(() => _isDirty = false)" />

<EditForm Model="@_model" OnValidSubmit="SaveAndCloseAsync">
    <TmTextInput @bind-Value="_model.Name"
        ValueChanged="@(v => { _model.Name = v; _isDirty = true; })" />
    <TmButton Type="ButtonType.Submit">Save</TmButton>
</EditForm>

@code {
    private TmNavigationGuard? _guard;
    private bool _isDirty;
    private DocumentModel _model = new();

    private async Task SaveAndCloseAsync()
    {
        await DocumentService.SaveAsync(_model);
        _isDirty = false;
        _guard?.Suppress();
        Navigation.NavigateTo("/documents");
    }
}
libraryExamples.setupNote: The beforeunload handler caches the dirty flag client-side and never calls back into .NET during unload, so it stays reliable even when the circuit is unloading. The guard only gates navigation — it does not manage locks or working copies.

libraryExamples.title: TmUserPicker - Generic picker with distinct empty vs transient-error states
libraryExamples.description: A generic entity picker (TUser) with debounced cancellable search and three explicit fetch states. A real network failure renders a retry-affordance error, never a silent "no results" message.
libraryExamples.code:
<TmUserPicker TUser="UserDto"
    @bind-Value="_ownerLogin"
    SearchProvider="SearchUsersAsync"
    ResolveProvider="ResolveUserAsync"
    ValueSelector="@(u => u.Login)"
    DisplaySelector="@(u => u.DisplayName)"
    Label="Owner"
    MinChars="2" />

@code {
    private string? _ownerLogin;

    private async Task<TmPickerSearchResult<UserDto>> SearchUsersAsync(string query, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        try
        {
            var users = await UserService.SearchAsync(query, ct);
            return new TmPickerSearchResult<UserDto>(users, users.Count == 0 ? TmPickerFetchState.Empty : TmPickerFetchState.Ok);
        }
        catch (Exception) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            // A real outage — must NOT render as "no results".
            return new TmPickerSearchResult<UserDto>([], TmPickerFetchState.Transient);
        }
    }

    private async Task<TmPickerResolveResult<UserDto>> ResolveUserAsync(string login, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var user = await UserService.GetByLoginAsync(login, ct);
        return new TmPickerResolveResult<UserDto>(user, TmPickerFetchState.Ok);
    }
}
libraryExamples.setupNote: SearchProvider/ResolveProvider are plain async functions — the component does not retry internally. If a caller wants retry-with-backoff before surfacing Transient, implement that inside the provider function itself.
